title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 3rd version, June 1986). M is a set of 'objects' (closed tame pieces, essentially closed cells or strata) ordered by inclusion ≤. Each object X has a boundary ∂X and an 'interior' X°. Judging from p.95, X° is the set of X' ≤ X with X' || ∂X, where || is a symmetric 'disjointness / transversality' relation. Supports are the closed sets of the Galois polarity defined by ||: Y || Supp(S) iff Y || every element of S. They form a lattice Σ_M with a canonical anti-involution C_M (orthocomplement). For an admissible family A (pairwise compatible objects, not necessarily closed under faces) Grothendieck sets S_A := Supp(⋃_{X∈A} X°), the support of the union of the open cells. The theorem on p.93 says that A ↦ S_A from subsets of F̃ (the cells of a 'complex' F) to Σ_M: (a) is an order-embedding; (b) commutes with arbitrary sups and infs; (c) sends set differences to S_A ∩ C_M(S_B); (d) for closed A gives the support of the underlying closed set. In other words, a closed subcomplex is the support of the union of its open cells, and the Boolean algebra of cell sets embeds into the support lattice.

On this page:
(1) He notes the statements are about operations on arbitrary admissible A, B, A_i.
(2) He checks the normalisation for A = F̃: S_F̃ = Supp(⋃ X°) = Supp F. Unwound through the polarity, this reads ∀Y: Y || F ⇔ ∀X∈F̃, Y || X°. He says it follows from the corollary to Lemma 1, i.e. a closed object is orthogonal-equivalent to the union of the open cells of its faces.
(3) He starts (a): S_A ⊂ S_B ⇒ A ⊂ B. Taking X ∈ A, this reduces to Supp(X°) ⊂ S_B ⇒ X ∈ B, stated as Lemma 8: if B ∪ {X} is admissible and X° ⊂ S_B, then X ∈ B.
(4) He starts unwinding the hypothesis: every Z with Z || ⋃_{Y∈B} Y° satisfies Z || X°.

The proof is finished on p.95 by contraposition. Take Z ∈ X°, which is nonempty by L1. By Lemma 4 (interiors of distinct objects are orthogonal), Z is orthogonal to all Y° with Y ∈ B, Y ≠ X. But Z is not orthogonal to X°. This is the standard argument that open cells are pairwise disjoint and nonempty, hence distinguish subcomplexes, recast in an axiomatic orthogonality framework.
errors: The written '$X^\circ \in S_B$' in Lemma 8 should be an inclusion $X^\circ \subset S_B$ (equivalently Supp(X°) ⊂ S_B). It is a notational slip, also present in the transcription.
Minor: Lemma 8 implicitly needs X° ≠ ∅ and Z not orthogonal to itself for nonzero Z. Both are supplied on p.95 via L1, so there is no real gap.

Next page (Lemma 4): the hypothesis 'X ≱ Y, X ≠ Y' looks partly superfluous. The proof handles both comparable cases symmetrically, so X ≠ Y alone suffices. This is either a slip or a transcription issue; it is not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Supports as closed sets of a Galois polarity given by a symmetric orthogonality relation ||, with a canonical anti-involution on the lattice of supports
ideas.modern_name: Polarity / orthogonality space closure (orthocomplemented lattice of biorthogonally closed sets)
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Analysis situs notes (156-x); the tame-topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) without this formalism

ideas.what: A closed cell complex equals the support of the union of its open cells; A ↦ S_A embeds the Boolean algebra of cell sets into the support lattice, preserving sup, inf and differences
ideas.modern_name: Correspondence between subcomplexes / unions of open strata and constructible-type subsets in a stratified or o-minimal cell decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical CW / stratification theory; o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries et al.)

ideas.what: Lemma 8 and its proof via disjointness and nonemptiness of open cells (Lemma 4, L1)
ideas.modern_name: Open cells of distinct cells are disjoint and nonempty

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 attempt to axiomatise tame topology lattice-theoretically: supports as polarity-closed sets of a disjointness relation with orthocomplement, and cell complexes embedded via open cells. Unlike o-minimality, this is not set-theoretic, and it is not documented in the tame-topology literature. Mathematically, though, the content of this page is routine.
missed.quote: $S_{\tilde F} \overset{def}{=} \mathrm{Supp}(\bigcup_{X \in \tilde F} X^\circ)$ ... Lemme 8 ... $X^\circ \in S_B \Rightarrow X \in B$
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' as a pointless / lattice-theoretic framework comparable to locales and o-minimal structures. No new theorem here.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification step (open cells distinguish subcomplexes) inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework itself is mildly interesting historically, but this page contains no notable new result.
transcription_corrections: '$X^\circ \in S_B$' is better read as $X^\circ \subset S_B$ (the intended meaning; the handwritten symbol is ambiguous).
'(n.p.s. $A = \tilde F$)' is uncertain; it probably means something like 'en particulier pour $A = \tilde F$'.

In '$\mathrm{Supp}\,F$' the F is struck through and the relation reads $Y \| F$ with F struck through (likely replaced by $\tilde F$, as in the line '$(Y \| \tilde F)$'), and the quantifier is '$\forall X \in \tilde F$'.
The last line reads 'considérant $\forall Z$ tel que $Z \| \bigcup_{Y \in B} Y^\circ$, on a $Z \| X^\circ$'. The X before ° is overwritten/struck in the image.
